The pin is deliberately self-invalidating: any later change to expected-script.hex must come back through this witness, whose spends re-EXECUTE the fixture's actual compiled locking script on the real @bsv/sdk Spend engine with real secp256k1 — which is why this fixture takes provenance path (A) rather than an allowlist hash. Both defects were reproduced by EXECUTION before the fix, not inferred: ecOnCurve(G||0xff) returned TRUE, ecPointX on a 32-byte blob succeeded, ecEncodeCompressed(G||0x01) flipped the compressed sign from 02 to 03, and ecAdd(G, allZero64) returned cf88213f...169139c6 with ecOnCurve(result) false. All seven independently written compilers regenerate these exact bytes; before each regeneration the conformance run reported 0 mismatches BETWEEN compilers against 70 unanimous golden mismatches, which is the signature of a correct port meeting a stale reference rather than a port bug. expected-ir.json is provably unmoved in both commits, so the ANF is untouched and only stack lowering changed.
